flag_definitions.historic_district: One or more properties in this jurisdiction may fall within a designated historic or landmark district. Historic/Landmarks Commission approval is required before building permits are issued. Adds 3–12 months to the timeline — verify with the local planning department before submitting.
flag_definitions.coastal: Project may fall within the California Coastal Zone. A Coastal Development Permit (CDP) from the California Coastal Commission is required in addition to local building permits. Verify parcel status at coastal.ca.gov/mycoast. CDP review can run concurrently with local permits if managed proactively.
flag_definitions.hillside: Hillside or sloped sites in this jurisdiction may trigger additional grading, geotechnical, and structural requirements. A soils/geotech report is typically required. Shoring or retaining wall permits may also apply.
flag_definitions.high_complexity: This is a high-complexity permitting jurisdiction with lengthy review timelines and multiple agencies involved. A licensed permit expediter is strongly recommended — not optional.
flag_definitions.adu_fast_track: California state law mandates a 60-day permit review for ADUs. Impact fees are waived for ADUs under 750 sqft. Pre-approved ADU plan sets may be available through the local AHJ to further accelerate permitting.
flag_definitions.hvhz: Miami-Dade High Velocity Hurricane Zone (HVHZ): all exterior products — windows, doors, roofing, and cladding — must carry a Miami-Dade Notice of Acceptance (NOA). Verify NOA compliance for every specified product before permit submission.
flag_definitions.owner_builder: Arkansas state law allows owner-builders to self-permit their primary residence. No contractor license is required. An owner-builder affidavit is signed at permit issuance. Subcontractors (electrician, plumber) must still be licensed.
flag_definitions.no_impact_fees: No school or park impact fees apply for remodels, additions, or ADUs in this jurisdiction — a meaningful cost advantage over California and other high-fee markets.
flag_definitions.fire_rebuild_fast_track: This jurisdiction has activated a dedicated fire rebuild permitting fast-track program. Confirm your project is registered in the fast-track queue and ask which fee waivers or timeline reductions apply to your parcel.

DPI must hold LADBS certification in relevant classification (RC, SM, SSW, GD, SFRM, MB, or WD). Hired and paid by property owner; coordinated by contractor.

clearances_required.notes: Verify no historic designation, specific plan restrictions, or HPOZ overlay.

demolition.typical_timeline: 2–8 weeks for permit issuance. Express permits (small/partial demo) can be same-day via PermitLA. Full demolition with clearances can take 4–12 weeks.
demolition.typical_fees: $200–$2,000+ depending on scope and structure size. Additional fees for hazmat abatement, SCAQMD compliance, and DPI services.

dpi_details.description: A Registered Deputy Inspector (DPI) is a licensed professional certified by LADBS to perform continuous or special inspections on behalf of the Department. For demolition, a DPI may be required when the scope involves structural elements, multi-story buildings, or work that could affect adjacent structures.
dpi_details.who_to_contact: Your assigned LADBS plan checker (first), LADBS Inspection Division at (213) 473-3231, or visit the Development Services Center at 201 N. Figueroa St., 4th Floor, Los Angeles, CA 90012.

key_forms.title: Registered Deputy Inspector's Certificate of Compliance
Employment and Duties of a Registered Deputy Inspector

dpi_details.hiring_process: The property owner (or their contractor) hires and pays for the DPI. The DPI performs continuous inspection during demolition, keeps records, and submits a Certificate of Compliance to LADBS and the design professional of record.
